reviews.notes: Accurately represents Arjuna's questions defining Brahma, Adhyātma, Karma, Adhibhūta, and Adhidaiva.
Directly matches Arjuna's second set of inquiries regarding Adhiyajña in the body and knowledge of the Lord at death.
Accurately captures Krishna's definitions of Akshara Brahman, Adhyatman as inner nature, and Karma as creative emanation.
Faithfully renders Adhibhuta (perishable nature), Adhidaiva (Purusha), and Krishna Himself as Adhiyajna in the physical body.
Matches antakāle ca māmeva smaran and attaining Krishna's divine being upon leaving the mortal frame.
Accurately captures attaining whatever state or object one meditates upon at the final moment of departure.
Directly renders the injunction to remember the Lord at all times and engage in battle (māmanusmara yudhya ca).
Accurately conveys attaining the Supreme Divine Purusha through unbroken yoga of practice and single-minded devotion.
Faithfully renders the attributes of the Ancient Sage, Ordainer of all, subtler than an atom, effulgent as the sun beyond all dark.
Accurately depicts the dying yogi focusing vital breath between the eyebrows with calm faith to reach the Supreme Person.
Corresponds to the imperishable goal (Aksharam) proclaimed by Vedic scholars, entered by dispassionate ascetics.
Directly matches controlling all sense gates, confining mind to the heart, and focusing prāṇa in meditative concentration.
Faithfully represents uttering the sacred monosyllable OM while departing in remembrance of Krishna.
Accurately represents the Lord being easily attained by the ever-steadfast yogi who remembers Him uninterruptedly.
Matches Mahatmas attaining the Lord and escaping rebirth in this fleeting abode of misery (duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam).
Accurately captures that all worlds up to Brahmaloka are subject to return, but reaching the Lord brings freedom from rebirth.
Directly renders the cosmic Day and Night of Brahma each spanning a thousand Yugas (sahasrayugaparyantam).
Faithfully presents the emergence of all manifested things at dawn and their dissolution back into the unmanifest at nightfall.
Accurately renders the multitude of beings helplessly dissolving at cosmic night and re-emerging at daybreak (bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate).
Corresponds to the higher unmanifest eternal Reality that never perishes even when all created beings perish.
Accurately represents the supreme unmanifest and imperishable state from which there is no return, as the Lord's supreme abode.
Faithfully renders the Supreme Purusha who pervades all and in whom all beings reside, attained by unswerving devotion.

chapterFindings: Verses 8.23 through 8.27 constitute a genuine five-verse source omission spanning ten Sanskrit hemistichs, correctly marked in the alignment with empty content and an explanatory note.
The source text anomaly wherein Gutenberg edition prints [FN#14] at the omission ellipsis instead of [FN#15] is faithfully noted without modifying the source text or corrupting the alignment.
Verses 8.9 and 8.10 are rendered in distinct four-line poetic stanzas with alternating rhyme, accurately corresponding to the respective canonical shlokas.
